title: Council Member Kelly King Town Hall with Lt. Governor Josh Green: February 23, 2021

recap.headline: COVID-19 town hall on Maui vaccine rollout, case trends and mask use
recap.in_60_seconds: South Maui Council Member Kelly King hosted a second COVID-19 webinar with Lt. Governor Josh Green, County Deputy Managing Director Josiah Nishita and State Representative Tina Wildberger. Officials said Maui cases were falling, but only 8.5% of Maui residents showed at least one vaccine dose. The Lt. Governor said 10,000 to 12,000 Maui doses had not yet been entered into the reporting system. Members of the public sent about a dozen questions by Zoom chat. They asked about vaccine priority for Maui, N95 masks, variants, mask enforcement and travel rules. Representative Wildberger announced twice-weekly vaccinations at the Kaiser clinic in Kīhei. No votes were taken, and a few questions, including one on House Bill 1286, got no clear answer on the recording.

parts.title: Welcome and overview
presented: This is the second COVID-19 town hall; questions are taken only through Zoom Q&A, with capacity raised to 500.
The U.S. passed 500,000 COVID deaths, about 20% of world deaths with about 4% of world population.
Maui County's 7-day case average fell from 35 in January to 16 on February 22.
8.5% of the county had at least one vaccine dose, behind the other counties.

next.what: Next town hall with U.S. Senator Brian Schatz

parts.title: Lt. Governor's update on cases, vaccines, variants and masks
presented: Hawaiʻi has the lowest infection rate in the nation; Maui had 202 cases in 14 days and 17 new cases that day.
312,000 vaccinations statewide; Maui shows 25,000, but 10,000 to 12,000 Maui doses are not yet entered in the system.
Maui got 4,840 doses in the latest shipment, about 10% of the state supply; the state is two-thirds through Phase 1b.
The state samples 75 cases a week for variants; KN95 masks work if they fit well.

next.what: Phases 2 and 3 for younger, lower-risk people

parts.title: County update on masks and testing
presented: Mask Up Maui County volunteers hand out free masks and explain the County rules; proper mask use fell from 96% in mid-January to about 91%.
Free County testing did about 23,600 tests from October 16 to February 21, with 512 positives (2.17%).
About 80% of positives were residents with no travel history; many cases are within large households.
18,000 to 20,000 County tests are still waiting to be reported to the Department of Health.

next.what: Groups wanting to join Mask Up Maui County can call the Office of the Mayor

parts.title: State Representative's question on vaccine help
presented: Asked if National Guard troops will come to Maui to speed vaccinations.
Noted Maui has 11.7% of the state population, not 10%.

answered.said: Guard help may very well come and money is available, but vaccine supply is the biggest limit.

raised.concern: Can Maui get priority for vaccine, given its higher case rate and more visitors?
What share must be vaccinated to return to normal, and will there be a vaccine passport?
Are N95 masks available to the public, and should they be handed out?
Disappointment that tourists go without masks.
Will vaccines be at pharmacies, and can people choose the type?
Is the variant sampling of 75 cases statewide or countywide?
Where on Maui are cases concentrated?
Who does the mask-wearing surveys and how is the data collected?

answered.said: He agrees Maui deserves more vaccine, but allocation also follows high-risk groups like care homes; supply will grow by about 50,000 extra doses plus Johnson & Johnson shots.
About 70% vaccinated brings much more normalcy, likely around July; apps could show vaccination status for events and travel.
N95s are good and no longer in national shortage; buying more is a good use of money. He asked lawmakers for a way to fine people without masks, since $5,000 fines or jail are not workable.
Yes, pharmacies are authorized, and people can choose their vaccine.
It is 75 cases a week statewide, about 300 a month; he asked for extra sampling on Maui.
Cases are mostly in Central Maui, with some more activity in South Maui.

answered.who: County Deputy Managing Director and Lieutenant Governor
answered.said: The Department of Health runs the surveys with volunteer observers and phone sampling, reported about weekly.
Sorting essential workers by paperwork is slow; an honor system for front-facing workers could speed vaccinations.

parts.title: South Maui vaccine clinic announcement
presented: Maui Health will give vaccines at the Kaiser clinic in Kīhei on Wednesdays and Fridays, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
This week is already full with rescheduled appointments; the service will run through the whole vaccine program.

next.what: Maui Health vaccine sign-up portal reopens

raised.concern: What is the Lt. Governor's stance on House Bill 1286 on uniform Safe Travels rules?
How will the state keep new variants from coming in, and why no statement on Safe Travels?
Large gatherings without masks at Kīhei beaches, and whether mask teams went to Kāʻanapali and Front Street.
Why is vaccine priority based on age when other risk factors matter?
Conditions in the COVID unit at Maui's hospital.
Kauaʻi data said 51% of positive travelers tested positive after arrival.

answered.said: Maui may need priority if high case rates continue; the low Maui count is mostly a reporting catch-up.
Maui has had only one variant case so far; a Kauaʻi-style shutdown is not possible; the state updates whenever a variant is found.
Law enforcement is a County role; he did not know if mask teams went to Kāʻanapali.
More gene sequencing would need costly machines; most states send samples to the CDC.
People over 85 are thousands of times more likely to die, so age stays the main factor.
He does not agree the COVID unit is bad; cases and deaths have been low.
He does not believe the Kauaʻi numbers are valid.
Enforcement uses education, Mask Up teams, community police officers, park rangers, and reports from residents.

parts.title: Closing remarks
presented: The Council Member urged wider use of N95 masks, which cost about $1.50 each in bulk.
The Lt. Governor expects at least 250,000 shots a month statewide and a much safer summer.
He said Hawaiʻi has had about 400 deaths and 27,270 cases, far below mainland rates.

next.what: Next webinar with U.S. Senator Brian Schatz, held midday

bills.name: Maui County public health emergency rules
bills.what: County rules that require face masks in public areas of Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi.

bills.name: House Bill 1286
bills.what: A state bill on uniform Safe Travels rules for arrivals.

open_questions.question: What is the Lt. Governor's position on House Bill 1286 on uniform Safe Travels rules?
Will National Guard troops come to Maui to speed vaccinations, and when?
What is being done about long phone hold times when people try to book vaccine appointments?
Did Mask Up teams go to Kāʻanapali and Front Street?
